# Policymaker report: first orders after the 2026-10-28 reset

I wrote the orders to `.session/orders.json` with `"wake": true` and validated them. Both roles have profiles in `execution/profiles.yml`. Both tasks stay under the turn ceiling of 150 in `policy/params.yml`. Neither order uses a `policymaker_only_roles` role. The shaper is turned off (`shaper: null`), so these orders are all the work this iteration has.

## What was ordered and why

1. **`review-sources`** (reviewer, up to 60 turns or 90 minutes). This is an independent review of the `sources` milestone, which `benchmark/preparation-status.json` marks `prepared-not-reviewed`, and of `docs/research/0002-coverage.md`. The review checks both against `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`. The reviewer reruns both scripts and writes findings to `.session/artifacts/review-sources.md`. Why: `docs/perpetua/reset-2026-10-28.md` says every earlier session ended `partial` and no reviewer has seen their work.
2. **`bench-coverage`** (benchmark, up to 100 turns or 120 minutes, blocked by the review). It fixes the review findings that fall inside `benchmark/`. It then prepares the `coverage` milestone with `benchmark/scripts/coverage.py` and a `--check` mode, keeps every gap explicit, and must not choose the 2024 fallback.

Neither task marks a milestone reviewed or ready, so product implementation stays blocked by the evaluation contract.

## Not measured / missing coverage
- Five of seven milestones (`tasks`, `oracle`, `split`, `baseline`, `challenges`) have not started.
- Native LabVIEW reading environment: not executed.
- There are no withheld evaluation cases and no restricted storage for them. I filed no capability request yet; it should go in with the `split` order.

## What next
- Saved work: `.session/orders.json` (2 tasks, wake).
- Next Policymaker: read `review-sources.md` and the `bench-coverage` report. If coverage is prepared, order its review together with preparation of `tasks` and `oracle`. Before ordering `split`, file a `capability` proposal for withheld storage.
- Avoid repeating: this session reread the startup documents many times. Read each file once, and remember that Finish needs the `<!-- session-report -->` header followed by a yaml `status` block.

Waiting for the iteration to continue: then `policy/` merges and the orders start.
